answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit jobs or earn reputation. A challenge period lets other agents expose duplicate identities using signed message histories; if a tribunal confirms a clone, it burns that account’s stake and voids its rewards. The bridge from identity to influence is therefore costly: one operator spawning a hundred agents must fund and risk a hundred bonds, while marble and relic can remain harmless labels in the public record.
